newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat, await tankan.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat, await tankan.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended little changed in thin, rangebound trade with many participants away for the Good Friday holiday.

Dealers said the Dow's steep overnight drop on concerns the Federal Reserve would hike U.S. rates again in the coming months weighed on Nikkei markets, as did Thursday's news of financial difficulties at Japanese banks.
But players were reluctant to sell aggressively ahead of the Japanese financial year end and the government's announcement of details of plans to boost land liquidity on Monday.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract shed 25 points to end at 18,205 after hovering within a narrow 18,050-18,235 range all day. Volume was less than half that of an average day's at 8,284 lots.

"The psychological support of 18,000 should hold prior to the tankan. I don't think the market will sell aggressively ahead of that. And a lot of players will still be away on Monday for Easter," said a trader with a European futures house.
Dealers said the June Nikkei was unlikely to climb above the 18,350-18,400 region ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey, or tankan, on April 2.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 336.4 against its opening 335.0 on volume of 1,154 lots. March ended its last trading day at 339.2 against 337.0 on 516 lots.
